content.text:
Reviewed `git diff origin/main...HEAD` (PR #391) from the reuse angle. Five findings.

---

**1. `internal/cli/transcript_store.go:101` — `excludedNow()` re-implements the session read guard**

It hand-builds `loadSessionTombstonesChecked` → `loadBrainManifest` → `excludedTranscriptPathsChecked`, then does an inline `excluded[rel]` path lookup at line ~283.

Use instead: `loadSessionReadGuard(brainDir, manifest)` (`internal/cli/session_privacy.go:513`), which already performs exactly that three-call sequence including the `len(stones.Excluded) == 0` short-circuit and the nil-manifest case, and already exposes path-blocking predicates (`blocksExportSession`, `blocksRecord`, `blocksFactAnchor`, `blocksFact` — `session_privacy.go:540-581`).

Cost: the tombstone gate is the one invariant this file exists to enforce, and it now has two independent implementations. The guard's five `blocks*` methods all key their path lookup through `normalizePrivacyTranscriptPath`; the store keys through its own `cleanTranscriptRel` (see finding 3), so the two can disagree on the same manifest. Any future widening of the gate (new durable artifact source, new path shape) must be made in both, and `policyIdentity` — the checked tombstone bytes the guard carries for auditing — is dropped on this path.

---

**2. `internal/cli/transcript_store.go:165-176` — third verbatim copy of the checkpoint-backend selection prelude**

`readEntireSettings` → `configuredCheckpointPrimary` → default to `checkpointBackendGitBranch` → reject malformed settings → `loadLocalCheckpointUnionSnapshot(..., localOnly=true)` is already written twice: `loadConfiguredCheckpointSnapshot` (`export.go:1530-1543`) and `loadLocalCheckpointSnapshotForVerify` (`verify_cmd.go:783-800`).

Use instead: `loadLocalCheckpointSnapshotForVerify`, generalized to take `raw bool, branchDestinations, cache` (it is already used outside verify — `entities_cmd.go:868` calls it for entity resolution, so it is the de-facto "local-only union snapshot for readers" helper; its name is the only thing verify-specific about it). The PR comment at line 159 correctly explains why `loadConfiguredCheckpointSnapshot` is wrong here, but that reasoning points straight at the verify helper, which already made the same choice for the same reason.

Cost: the env-then-local-then-base precedence contract documented on `configuredCheckpointPrimary` now has three call sites to keep in sync; a new backend type or a change to the "unconfigured defaults to git-branch" rule silently diverges in one of them.

---

**3. `internal/cli/transcript_store.go:238` — `cleanTranscriptRel` is a fourth brain-relative path normalizer**

`path.Clean(strings.ReplaceAll(rel, "\\", "/"))` with an empty/"." reject.

Use instead: `normalizePrivacyTranscriptPath` (`session_privacy.go:304`) — same contract (trim, clean, reject "."), and it is the function that produces the keys of the very map this value is looked up in. Where safety matters (the `Open` path), `cleanBrainRelativePath` (used by `openCanonicalHistoryTranscript` at `history_input.go:444` and by `privacyTransactionTranscriptPaths` at `session_privacy.go:1207`) is the validated form.

Cost: `cleanTranscriptRel` and `normalizePrivacyTranscriptPath` disagree on backslash input (`ReplaceAll` to `/` vs `filepath.FromSlash`, which is a no-op on Unix), so a manifest path containing a backslash produces a gate key that the store's lookup cannot hit. Also means three normalizers now guard one namespace.

---

**4. `internal/cli/export.go:3196` — `budgetedTranscriptRead` hand-formats the size-bound error**

`fmt.Errorf("transcript %s exceeds maximum size of %d bytes", path, maxBytes)` reproduces, as a string, the message of an existing typed error.

Use instead: `&readBoundExceededError{source: "transcript " + path, max: maxBytes}` (`safe_read.go:154`), which exists precisely so size refusals are distinguishable via `errors.As` from I/O errors and cancellation — see the comment at `safe_read.go:150` and the consumer at `conversation.go:692`.

Cost: the new budget error is only detectable by substring matching. `transcriptStore.Open` wraps it (`"read transcript %s: %w"`) and returns it before `Read`'s own `strings.Contains(..., "exceeds maximum size")` check at `transcript_store.go:252` ever runs, so a git-backed oversized transcript does not get classified as `memoryErrInputTooLarge` the way the file-backed one does — the two branches of the same store return different error classes for the same condition.

---

**5. `internal/cli/transcript_store.go:86` — hardcoded `ExecRunner{}` bypasses the injected command-runner seam**

`transcriptStoreFor` constructs every process-wide store with `ExecRunner{}`, while `newTranscriptStore` already accepts a `CommandRunner`.

Use instead: the `Options.Runner` seam that every other git-touching helper threads (`root.go:45` sets it; `entities_cmd.go:868` and `verify_cmd.go:715` both pass `opts.Runner` into the identical snapshot call). `readCanonicalHistoryTranscript` would need a runner parameter, or the store needs a registration point fed from `Options`.
